resources.string: I’m wysie. I maintain Zeekr Companion, a fork of Zeekr Shortcut by dts88. I use it primarily for my ZEEKR 009, with my own improvements, experiments and contributions adapted from the open-source community.
Projects and downloads

My source code and downloads are linked below, alongside dts88’s original project and Ferix’s CAMCORDER project. For issues with Zeekr Companion, please use my repository and attach a report from Settings → System → Diagnostics.
About USB drives

Recordings and photos are saved to your selected storage. With relay writing enabled, finished clips are buffered in the app’s private internal storage before transfer to USB. Developer options can also allow internal recording.

• Use the vehicle’s designated dashcam/Sentry storage port. Other ports may lose power after you leave; check that your selected drive remains available.

• A missing or slow drive can interrupt recording. Internal relay buffers are retained for retry, but clearing app data or uninstalling removes them.

• Do not remove a drive while files are being written or transferred. Check important recordings on another device.
Privacy and network use

Recordings and photos are stored locally. The app does not upload them. The selected storage and private relay buffers may contain unencrypted footage. Anyone who can access those files can read them.

Network features run when you request them:

• Check for updates: queries GitHub and, after your confirmation, downloads the APK. No vehicle diagnostics or recordings are uploaded.

• Send to phone: temporarily shares the selected file over your local network until you close the sharing window. Anyone with the active link on that network can download it.

Exported diagnostics and settings backups can contain vehicle details, locations or file paths. Review them before sharing.
Safety notice
Experimental, unofficial software, not affiliated with ZEEKR. While driving, watch the road, not this app. Recordings are not guaranteed to be complete. Use at your own risk.

The original project also thanks its users, ZEEKR and Geely.
Credits and open source

Thank you to dts88 for creating the original Zeekr Shortcut and the foundation this edition builds on. For the original, more thoroughly tested version, please use dts88’s releases. My edition has more limited vehicle testing.

Thank you to suyunkai and the EVCam contributors for the underlying camera, recording and floating-window foundations. This edition remains open source under GNU GPL v3.0; source and attribution are available in the project repository.
